newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO take Jerusalem battle to classrooms.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO take Jerusalem battle to classrooms.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinian Authority have taken their battle over Jerusalem into the classrooms with Israel announcing it will supervise a matriculation exam for Palestinian high school students.
Chief Palestinian lawmaker Ahmed Korei on Wednesday attacked the decision, calling it a serious escalation of measures to tighten Israel's grip on the Arab half of the city.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, speaking at a ceremony on Wednesday marking the 30th anniversary of its capture of East Jerusalem, pledged that East Jerusalem would remain under Israeli sovereignty.
The Israeli government-sponsored exam will be held later this month.

"You have heard about the Israeli ministerial committee which has decided to impose Israeli curriculum on Jerusalem schools and that the matriculation exams will be under Israeli supervision," Korei told a news conference in Ramallah.
"This violates all the logic, text and spirit of the agreements reached with the Israeli government," Korei said.
A spokesman for the Israeli municipality of Jerusalem accused the Palestinian Authority of trying to take over the school system.
Spokesman Hagai Elias confirmed the city council would supervise exams in municipal-run schools but said he had not heard about changes to the curriculum.
"There are schools that Jerusalem municipality is running and we say we will sponsor the exam and will not let anyone interfere," said spokemsan Hagai Elias.
Since its occupation of East Jerusalem in 1967, Israel has maintained the Jordanian curriculum in schools run by its municipality. It also allowed Palestinians to retain Jordanian citizenship.
Palestinians said there were 101 schools in East Jerusalem, 34 of which are run by Israel, while the remainder are run privately or by a United Nations refugee agency.
Korei said the 88-member Palestinian legislative council had rejected the Israeli move as illegal and called on students to refuse Israeli supervision.
Korei said Israel's decision was an attempt to tighten its grip on the city, which the sides under a 1993 self-rule accord had agreed to discuss in talks on a permanent peace deal.
"Over the past two days, Israel has stepped up its measures to Judaise Jerusalem. These measures come in the shadow of a dangerous situation facing the peace process," Korei said.
"Israel has no rights over the schools or the education in East Jerusalem," Korei said.
Netanyahu announced on Wednesday that more police would be stationed to in East Jerusalem to tighten Israel's security grip there.
